findings.source_passage: Is it not a saying in every one's mouth, Possession is half of the law: that is, regardless of how the thing came into possession? But often possession is the whole of the law.
findings.source_locator: paragraph beginning 'Is it not a saying in every one's mouth'
findings.why_it_matters: The rhetorical build-up — the familiar adage invoked and then immediately exceeded ('But often possession is the whole of the law') — is a signature ironic move that gives the subsequent Fast-Fish catalogue its full satirical force. The draft collapses this to 'Possession is half the law? Oft it is the whole,' losing the deliberate rhetorical cadence and the echo of the adage.
findings.suggested_fix: Restore the source phrasing: 'Is it not a saying in every one's mouth, Possession is half of the law: that is, regardless of how the thing came into possession? But often possession is the whole of the law.' before the Fast-Fish catalogue.

findings.source_passage: and concerning all these, is not Possession the whole of the law?
findings.source_locator: end of the Fast-Fish catalogue paragraph
findings.why_it_matters: This closing rhetorical question caps the entire Fast-Fish catalogue and reinforces the chapter's central jurisprudential irony; its omission leaves the catalogue without its structural coda.
findings.suggested_fix: Append 'And concerning all these, is not Possession the whole of the law?' at the end of the Fast-Fish list.

findings.source_passage: A common man looking at this decision of the very learned Judge, might possibly object to it.
findings.source_locator: paragraph beginning 'A common man looking at this decision'
findings.why_it_matters: This sentence establishes the narrator's ironic populist stance before pivoting to the jurisprudential abstraction; its absence slightly dulls the tonal shift from legal comedy to philosophical polemic.
findings.suggested_fix: Insert 'A common man looking at this decision of the very learned Judge, might possibly object to it. But ploughed up to the primary rock…' to preserve the ironic setup.

summary: The draft is largely faithful, preserving nearly all key signatures verbatim, but slightly flattens the pivotal 'Possession is half of the law' rhetorical turn and drops its closing cap, causing minor but measurable voice loss at the hinge between legal comedy and satirical polemic.
